## Definition check

The sentence from **“Source rubric and schema paths (#158)”**, verbatim and in full:

> Read release-specific notes from the dedicated `updates.update_details` field, `updates.description` or `notes`, requiring actual release or derivation information rather than crediting unrelated notes.

This is consistent with the current rules, so I proceeded. Recorded `instrument_sha256` as `66ad6231…34864`.

## Result — CM4AI, claudecode_api, rep1

**39 / 47 adjusted = 82.98%** · **39 / 50 fixed = 78.0%** · 3 sub-elements N/A

| El | Score | El | Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Discovery | 5/5 | 6 Provenance/Version | 5/5 |
| 2 Access | 5/5 | 7 Motivation/Funding | 5/5 |
| 3 Reuse | 3/5 | 8 Technical Transparency | 3/5 |
| 4 Ethics | 2/2 | 9 Limitations | 3/5 |
| 5 Composition | 3/5 | 10 Community | 5/5 |

**Applicability.** Element 4 is gated per sub-element. The human-subjects condition fails on *external* evidence — E1's description and keywords name MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J cell lines and reagents; E8's `collection_mechanisms` describes mass spectrometry, confocal microscopy and CRISPRi screens, not recruitment; `direct_collection` states data were not collected from individuals. So sub-elements 3–5 (participant privacy, consent, vulnerable populations) are `applicable: false`, `score: null`, denominator 47. Sub-elements 1–2 *are* scored, because the governance disjunct fires on E2 evidence: an operative pre-publication embargo, a commercial-use restriction naming UCSD/Stanford/UCSF, and a named Data Governance Committee contact. Both scored 1. All other gates (datasets-shared; collection identified; software-output for E8.3) are satisfied.

**Element 8 sub-element 4 scored 0** under the #1082 threshold. The record names software, but none of it produced or transformed the released data: the Cell Mapping Toolkit's output — computed cell maps — is stated by the record itself to be excluded from this release (role e); FAIRSCAPE is packaging and provenance-metadata software (role c); the 10x 3′HT kit is capture instrumentation (role a). What generated the perturbation atlas, the MS outputs and the image archives is unstated. Per #1081 the sub-element was still scored rather than excluded — gating it on a repository pointer would excuse the record by its own silence.

**Other zeros:** formats stop at the ZIP container with no interior format or encoding (3.2); no `variables` at all (3.4, 5.3); no instance counts asserted — every available figure is explicitly disclaimed (5.2); preprocessing documented only as an inference from filenames (8.3); no data-level quality/anomaly reporting, only metadata anomalies (9.3); no social-impact analysis (9.5).

Notable: this record's extensive `source_caveats` discipline causes several of these zeros — it declines to assert figures it cannot support. I credited that as a strength in the assessment but did not let it earn points for content that isn't there. Two consistency failures (temporal ordering; portal/Dataverse release-year conflict) and six warnings recorded; DOI, both NIH grant numbers, RRIDs and URLs all validate.
